title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed from this page and its neighbours). Sigma is a structure the page calls 'un [?]'; the word is illegible, possibly 'partitif' or a 'treillis de partitions'. It behaves like a complete lattice equipped with:
- a disjointness relation x|0|y, read 'x and y are disjoint', i.e. inf(x,y)=0;
- a complement C, with eta|0|xi iff eta <= C(xi).
From a set E with a map sigma: E -> Sigma, Grothendieck builds a 'completion' Sigma_E. A subset E' of E (or of Sigma) is called dense if every element is the sup of the elements of E' below it.

The proposition being proved has conditions (i)-(v); its proof spans pp. 81-83. The previous page proved (i) <=> (iv) <=> (v).
- (iv) says sigma(E') is order-dense in sigma(E).
- (v) says: for all x, y in E, if x'|0|y' holds for all x' <= x and y' <= y taken in E', then x|0|y.

Lemma on this page. Let Sigma be as above, E a dense part, S' a subset of Sigma bounded by xi (so Sup S' <= xi). Then Sup S' = xi if and only if, for every eta in E, S'|0|eta implies xi|0|eta.

Proof.
- Necessity is already known: if Sup S' = xi, then for all eta, S'|0|eta <=> xi|0|eta.
- Sufficiency, step 1: S'|0|eta means eta <= Inf_{xi' in S'} C(xi'), and xi|0|eta means eta <= C(xi). So the hypothesis says that every eta in E below Inf C(xi') is below C(xi).
- Step 2: by density, Inf C(xi') is the sup of the elements of E below it. Hence Inf_{xi' in S'} C(xi') <= C(xi).
- Step 3: complementing, xi <= C(Inf C(xi')) = Sup CC(xi') = Sup xi'. Hence xi = Sup S'.

Use in the argument. The lemma completes the equivalence of (i), (iv) and (v). Grothendieck then notes that, given Prop. 1, condition (v) says the canonical injection E' in E -> Sigma_E identifies Sigma_E with Sigma_{E'}, i.e. a dense part has the same completion. The identification is given one way by the map beta of Prop. 2, via (ii), and conversely by alpha, via (iii); the next page continues this.

In modern terms, this is the elementary theory of the completion of a 'separative' disjointness structure. Examples are the complete Boolean algebra of polars or regular open sets, the Boolean completion of a forcing poset, and the lattice of closed sets of an orthogonality space. The specific fact that a dense subset generates the same completion is standard.
errors: The step from Inf C(xi') <= C(xi) to xi <= Sup xi' silently uses that C is an order-reversing involution satisfying De Morgan (C(Inf a_i) = Sup C(a_i), CC = id). That is, Sigma is assumed Boolean, or at least an ortholattice with C an involution. With only a pseudocomplement one gets only xi <= CC(Sup S'), which is the regular-element closure of Sup S'. Presumably the axioms of Sigma, defined on earlier pages, guarantee this; it is not justified on this page.
In the statement, 'Sup S' <= xi' is written as an equivalent ('i.e.') of 'formed of elements majorized by xi'. That is correct but trivial. No real error otherwise.

ideas.what: Criterion for a sup via disjointness tested on a dense subset: Sup S' = xi iff every element of the dense part E disjoint from S' is disjoint from xi.
ideas.modern_name: Sup criterion in a complete Boolean algebra / ortholattice via orthogonal complements on a dense (join-generating) subset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard Boolean-algebra and forcing folklore (Stone, Tarski; MacNeille completion; Scott-Solovay Boolean-valued models, 1960s)

ideas.what: A dense subset E' of E yields the same completion: Sigma_{E'} is identified with Sigma_E via the canonical injection.
ideas.modern_name: Dense embeddings induce isomorphic Boolean completions (regular open algebra of a separative poset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Forcing theory (Cohen, Solovay, Scott, Vopenka); orthogonality spaces (Dacey, Foulis-Randall)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine lattice-theoretic lemma (a sup criterion through complements and density) inside a 1986 axiomatic treatment of disjointness structures. The mathematics is standard (Boolean completions, dense embeddings). The only mild historical interest is that Grothendieck was developing such an order/disjointness formalism in 1986; the lemma itself is not new.
transcription_corrections: Final paragraph: 'les conditions (iii) (iv) (v) de la propos.' should very likely read '(i) (iv) (v)'. The previous page proved (i)<=>(iv)<=>(v), and the next page speaks of '(i) (ou ses variantes (iv), (v))'.
'Comme le dernier[?] des propriétés[?] prop. 1' is more plausibly 'Compte tenu des propriétés [de la] prop. 1'.
'l'application canonique E' ⊂ E → Σ_E' is probably 'l'injection canonique'.
The opening line reads 'Lemme Soient Σ un [?]'. The illegible word is possibly 'partitif' or similar; the next page has 'un [?] partitions'.
Page numbers: '82' at the top is Grothendieck's numbering; '85' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
